title: Quadratic Formula
description: Finds the roots of the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0

title: Difference of Squares
description: Factoring identity expressing the difference of two perfect squares as a product

title: Sum of Cubes
description: Factoring identity for the sum of two perfect cubes

title: Binomial Theorem
description: Expands any power of a binomial as a sum using binomial coefficients

title: Arithmetic Progression Sum
description: Sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic sequence with first term a and common difference d

title: Geometric Progression Sum
description: Sum of the first n terms of a geometric sequence with first term a and common ratio r ≠ 1

title: Laws of Exponents
description: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents

title: Logarithm Change of Base
description: Converts a logarithm of any base to natural logarithms (or any other base)

title: Circle Area
description: Area enclosed by a circle of radius r

title: Pythagorean Theorem
description: Relates the three sides of a right triangle, where c is the hypotenuse

title: Triangle Area
description: Area of a triangle with base b and perpendicular height h

title: Volume of Sphere
description: Volume enclosed by a sphere of radius r

title: Volume of Cylinder
description: Volume of a right circular cylinder with radius r and height h

title: Heron's Formula
description: Area of a triangle from side lengths a, b, c where s = (a+b+c)/2 is the semi-perimeter

title: Arc Length
description: Length of a circular arc subtended by central angle θ (in radians) in a circle of radius r

title: Ellipse Area
description: Area enclosed by an ellipse with semi-major axis a and semi-minor axis b

title: Pythagorean Identity
description: Fundamental identity relating sine and cosine, derived from the Pythagorean theorem on the unit circle

title: Double Angle (Sine)
description: Expresses the sine of a double angle in terms of sine and cosine of the original angle

title: Double Angle (Cosine)
description: Expresses the cosine of a double angle in terms of cosine and sine of the original angle

title: Law of Cosines
description: Generalises the Pythagorean theorem to any triangle, relating all three sides and one angle

title: Euler's Formula
description: Fundamental relationship between complex exponentials and trigonometric functions

title: Sum-to-Product (Sine)
description: Converts the sum of two sines into a product of sine and cosine

title: Tangent Addition
description: Expresses the tangent of a sum of two angles in terms of the tangents of those angles

title: Power Rule
description: Differentiation rule for power functions; reduces the exponent by one and multiplies by the original exponent

title: Product Rule
description: Differentiates the product of two functions u and v

title: Chain Rule
description: Differentiates a composite function by multiplying the outer derivative by the inner derivative

title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
description: Connects differentiation and integration: the definite integral equals the net change in any antiderivative F

title: Integration by Parts
description: Transforms the integral of a product into a simpler integral, analogous to the product rule for derivatives

title: Taylor Series
description: Represents a smooth function as an infinite sum of polynomial terms around point a

title: L'Hôpital's Rule
description: Evaluates indeterminate limits (0/0 or ∞/∞) by differentiating numerator and denominator separately

title: Mean
description: Arithmetic average of a dataset; sum of all values divided by the count

title: Variance
description: Measures how spread out values are around the mean; average of squared deviations

title: Standard Deviation
description: Square root of the variance; expressed in the same units as the data

title: Normal Distribution PDF
description: Probability density function of the Gaussian (normal) distribution with mean μ and standard deviation σ

title: Bayes' Theorem
description: Updates the probability of hypothesis A given new evidence B, using prior probabilities
